prompts.text: I believe the feasibility check "can capacity c finish in d days" is monotonic in c, so binary search over capacities between max(weight) and sum(weights) finds the smallest feasible one in O(n log sum). Review my reasoning without giving me the implementation. What would break it?

learn.title: 1 · Problem
learn.md: Packages with weights `weights[i]` must be shipped **in order** within `days` days. Each day the ship is loaded with consecutive packages up to a capacity. Return the **least capacity** that ships everything within `days` days.

learn.title: 2 · Clarifications
learn.md:
- Must packages stay in order? (Yes.)
- Can a package exceed the capacity? (No — so the lower bound is the heaviest package.)
- Can the total exceed int? (Yes — use long for the sum.)

learn.title: 3 · Key insight
learn.md: You cannot compute the answer directly, but you can check one guess in O(n). And the check is monotonic — if capacity c works, every larger capacity works — so binary-search the answer itself.

learn.title: 4 · Approach

learn.title: 12 · Common AI mistakes
learn.md:
- Starting the search at 1 instead of the heaviest package (wastes iterations and miscounts days).
- int overflow summing weights or in (lo + hi) / 2.
- Off-by-one in the loop bounds (lo < hi vs lo <= hi) producing an infinite loop.
- Linear search over capacities.
